Subject: Follow-up: data handling, console logs & breach-notify sequencing (post-demo)

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning, Alex — appreciate the time. Quick recap and next steps on the privacy/data items we flagged so your security and legal teams have what they need to qualify Redwood for the pilot.

High-level recap
- Scope: MedSync will send clinical summaries and user-entered form data (PII/PHI) into Redwood for model-assisted summarization.
- Residency: Some EU patients; you asked whether we can guarantee EU data residency for certain workloads.
- Logging: you want console/request logs retained for audit; curious about granularity and retention windows.
- Subprocessors & breach notify: you asked for the subprocessors list and how Redwood handles breach notifications (timing, timeline deliverables).

What we attached
- redwood-dpa-summary.pdf — short explainer of standard DPA roles and common addendum options.
- redwood-subprocessors-2028-06.csv — current registry export (service+region+purpose).

Questions / asks from MedSync (please confirm in reply)
1) Confirm role: is MedSync expecting Redwood to be Processor under the DPA for the pilot?
2) Residency: do you require 100% EU residency for requests tied to EU patients, or is a hybrid arrangement acceptable?
3) Retention: target retention for console/request logs for audit purposes (default on hosted is 90 days).
4) Breach notification expectations: you mentioned a 30-day notify requirement in your contract templates — can you confirm whether you need Redwood to commit to a specific notify window in the addendum?

Proposed next steps
- If you confirm role/residency/retention, I’ll loop in Legal to draft a DPA addendum reflecting those options.
- I can provision a test tenant with EU residency for a short pilot if you want to validate data residency and logs.
- If you want a tighter notify SLA (e.g., 30 days or specific timeline), call that out and we’ll show what’s possible in an enterprise addendum.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short email to legal with the specifics once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, console logs & breach-notify sequencing (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. Answers inline below.

1) Role: yes, MedSync will treat Redwood as Processor for the pilot. We control prompts and mapping; Redwood processes on our behalf.

2) Residency: for EU patients we need EU data residency for storage and model execution for those specific requests. Hybrid is acceptable for non-EU requests but EU data must remain in EU regions.

3) Retention: security wants a minimum of 180 days for console/request logs (audit + correlation). Is extending beyond your default possible or does that require Dedicated/Private?

4) Breach notification: our legal prefers notification within 72 hours of detection and a timeline of remediation steps delivered within 30 days. We understand timelines vary by investigation, but want a contractual commitment for initial notify + follow-up timeline.

Additional ask: can you confirm whether Redwood pseudonymizes input PII at rest (tokenization/pseudonymization) for stored artifacts? Also please include any SOC 2 certs/attestation or pen-test summaries we can share with InfoSec.

If it helps, I can have our attorney (cc'd security@medsync.com) share the clause language that drives the 72h notify / 30-day timeline ask.

Regards,
Alex
Head of Platform
MedSync Health
[signature]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 10:45:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, console logs & breach-notify sequencing (post-demo)

Appreciate the clear answers, Alex — helpful. Quick responses and what we can provide next.

Role: noted (Redwood = Processor). We’ll reflect that in the addendum.

Residency: we can provision EU-only execution and storage for identified requests. For the pilot we can enable an EU tenant (isolated region) and route EU-labeled requests there — I'll include provisioning instructions in the follow-up.

Retention / Logs: hosted default is 90 days. We can offer 180 days for request/console logs as an addendum option (no Dedicated requirement for logs-only extension, though there is a cost delta we will show). For full forensic data exports beyond 180 days we typically require a Dedicated/Private contract.

Breach notify: Redwood's standard commitment is initial notification within 48 hours of confirmed incident and we provide an incident timeline and remediation plan as it is developed. For enterprise addenda we can incorporate a 72-hour initial notification clause instead if that aligns better with your legal team, and include a target for a 30-day remediation timeline for straightforward incidents. For complex investigations we keep regular updates.

Pseudonymization: we support application-level pseudonymization patterns (customer-controlled tokenization). Redwood does not automatically pseudonymize all ingested content at rest by default because customers need their original data for model quality; we can offer tokenization for specific fields as part of the onboarding configuration.

Evidence pack: copying a link to SOC2 Type II and latest pen test report here — security can download directly: https://redwoodinference.com/security/soc2-2028-type2.pdf

Next steps / proposed plan
- I will ask Legal to draft a tailored DPA addendum that: (a) marks Redwood as Processor, (b) includes EU-residency option for pilot, (c) sets logs retention to 180 days, (d) includes a 72h initial notify + 30-day remediation target, and (e) enumerates available pseudonymization options.
- Ben (CC) will confirm any pricing implications for 180-day retention and EU tenancy.
- If that sounds good, we can send the addendum for review and route it through DocuSign for signature.

Would you like me to include your attorney's clause language when I open the ticket with Legal?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf (pdf)]
